phrase: X can mean different things to different people.
usage: Introducing a topic that has many perspectives.
example: Success can mean different things to different people.
vietnamese: X có thể mang ý nghĩa khác nhau với mỗi người.

phrase: For one person, it may mean X, whereas for someone else it may mean Y.
usage: Contrasting two different viewpoints or situations.
example: For one person, it may mean earning a high salary, whereas for someone else it may mean having free time.
vietnamese: Với người này, nó có thể là X, trong khi với người khác nó có thể là Y.

usage: Citing evidence to support an argument. Great for IELTS Writing Task 2.
example: Research suggests that regular exercise improves mental health.
vietnamese: Nghiên cứu cho thấy / Nghiên cứu gợi ý rằng…

phrase: It isn't necessarily what you might have thought.
usage: Challenging a common assumption.
example: The answer to the problem isn't necessarily what you might have thought.
vietnamese: Nó không nhất thiết là những gì bạn nghĩ.

usage: A rhetorical question to introduce analysis. Strong opening for essays or presentations.
example: What makes a good leader a good leader?
vietnamese: Điều gì khiến X là X?

phrase: …make a far greater contribution to X than Y.
usage: Comparing the importance of two factors.
example: Soft skills make a far greater contribution to career success than technical knowledge alone.
vietnamese: …đóng góp lớn hơn nhiều cho X so với Y.

phrase: That doesn't mean that… It just means that…
usage: Clarifying a point to avoid misunderstanding.
example: That doesn't mean that technology is bad. It just means that we need to use it wisely.
vietnamese: Điều đó không có nghĩa là… Chỉ là…

usage: Adding a surprising or emphatic piece of evidence.
example: In fact, most successful entrepreneurs failed multiple times before succeeding.
vietnamese: Thực tế, …

usage: Highlighting what makes something unique.
example: What distinguishes great teachers is that they inspire curiosity.
vietnamese: Điều phân biệt X là…

usage: Acknowledging something before presenting a deeper point.
example: This might seem obvious, but many people still underestimate the value of sleep.
vietnamese: Điều này có vẻ hiển nhiên, nhưng…

phrase: The implications are greater than you might think.
usage: Emphasizing that something has bigger consequences than expected.
example: Climate change is accelerating — the implications are greater than you might think.
vietnamese: Những hệ quả lớn hơn bạn nghĩ.

phrase: Not only X but also Y.
usage: Adding emphasis by listing multiple effects. Very useful in IELTS Writing.
example: Exercise benefits not only your body but also your mind.
vietnamese: Không chỉ X mà còn Y.

phrase: There is some evidence to support / suggest that…
usage: Presenting evidence cautiously — good academic writing style.
example: There is some evidence to suggest that bilingual children develop stronger problem-solving skills.
vietnamese: Có bằng chứng cho thấy / gợi ý rằng…

usage: Contrasting a better approach with a less helpful one.
example: Try to learn from mistakes rather than focusing on failure.
vietnamese: …thay vì tập trung vào X.

usage: A strong, natural way to disagree or deny something.
example: Does that mean we should give up? Not at all.
vietnamese: Hoàn toàn không.

phrase: But overall it seems that it is X that…
usage: Summarizing a main conclusion. Great for essay conclusions.
example: But overall it seems that it is consistent effort that leads to long-term success.
vietnamese: Nhưng nhìn chung, dường như chính X là điều…

phrase: This is something that you can work on in your daily life.
usage: Encouraging action — a practical, motivational closing statement.
example: Confidence is something that you can work on in your daily life.
vietnamese: Đây là điều bạn có thể rèn luyện mỗi ngày.

usage: A powerful closing that puts responsibility on the reader/listener.
example: You have the tools and the knowledge. It's up to you.
vietnamese: Tùy thuộc vào bạn.

phrase: There are still legitimate concerns about…
usage: Acknowledging a valid opposing viewpoint before presenting your argument. Great for balanced IELTS essays.
example: There are still legitimate concerns about the impact of social media on teenagers.
vietnamese: Vẫn còn những lo ngại chính đáng về…

usage: Introducing a growing trend in research. Shows academic awareness.
example: Scientists are increasingly examining the link between sleep quality and productivity.
vietnamese: Các nhà khoa học ngày càng nghiên cứu / xem xét…

usage: Presenting research findings as evidence.
example: Their studies are revealing that regular exercise can reduce anxiety by up to 50%.
vietnamese: Các nghiên cứu cho thấy rằng…

usage: Pointing out an unresolved question in research. Shows critical thinking.
example: Still unclear is whether online learning is as effective as classroom learning.
vietnamese: Điều chưa rõ là liệu…

usage: Explaining why something is well-suited for a purpose.
example: Its interactive design makes the app ideal for language learning.
vietnamese: X khiến Y trở nên lý tưởng cho…

usage: Describing a solution or innovation.
example: Researchers have figured out a way to recycle plastic more efficiently.
vietnamese: …đã tìm ra cách để…

phrase: X have been shown, in separate studies, to…
usage: Citing multiple sources of evidence. Strong academic writing.
example: Green spaces have been shown, in separate studies, to reduce stress and improve mood.
vietnamese: X đã được chứng minh, qua các nghiên cứu riêng biệt, là…

usage: Connecting new evidence to existing knowledge.
example: These findings fit with earlier research on the benefits of outdoor play.
vietnamese: Những phát hiện này phù hợp với…

phrase: The jury is still out on whether…
usage: Expressing that something is still undecided. Natural idiom for discussions.
example: The jury is still out on whether artificial intelligence will create or destroy jobs.
vietnamese: Vẫn chưa có kết luận liệu…

usage: Describing broad improvement across multiple areas.
example: Students who joined the program improved on a wide range of academic skills.
vietnamese: …cải thiện ở nhiều khía cạnh / lĩnh vực…

phrase: boost mental function / boost brain power
usage: Collocation: verb + noun. Talking about cognitive improvement.
example: Regular reading can boost mental function and improve concentration.
vietnamese: tăng cường chức năng trí não / sức mạnh não bộ

usage: Collocation: talking about positive social impact of an activity.
example: Team sports encourage prosocial behaviors like cooperation and empathy.
vietnamese: khuyến khích hành vi vì xã hội

phrase: have a physical effect on the body / brain
usage: Collocation: describing measurable physical changes.
example: Meditation has been shown to have a physical effect on the brain, reducing cortisol levels.
vietnamese: có tác động vật lý lên cơ thể / não bộ

usage: Collocation: discussing whether skills transfer to real life.
example: The question is whether problem-solving skills from puzzles can be applied to real-world tasks.
vietnamese: áp dụng (kết quả/kỹ năng) vào các nhiệm vụ ngoài trò chơi

usage: Collocation: describing determination and resilience.
example: Successful students persist at solving challenging problems instead of giving up.
vietnamese: kiên trì giải quyết các vấn đề khó

usage: A common idiom meaning something has both positive and negative aspects. Very useful in IELTS essays.
example: Technology is a double-edged sword — it connects people but can also isolate them.
vietnamese: Đây là con dao hai lưỡi.

usage: Describing a system of incentives and consequences.
example: Good education systems reward effort and punish dishonesty.
vietnamese: …thưởng một số hành động và phạt các hành động khác.

phrase: The challenge for X will be figuring out how to…
usage: Identifying a future challenge. Good for conclusions in IELTS essays.
example: The challenge for governments will be figuring out how to balance economic growth with environmental protection.
vietnamese: Thách thức cho X sẽ là tìm cách…

usage: Use to highlight the most popular or impressive feature of a place.
example: The top attraction is Penguin Island, home to a diverse array of wildlife.
vietnamese: Điểm thu hút hàng đầu là…

usage: Use to describe something a place is proud of or famous for.
example: The island boasts the largest colony of penguins in Western Australia.
vietnamese: tự hào có [đặc điểm ấn tượng]

usage: Use to describe how a place or route can be reached.
example: A 500 m walk trail along the Serpentine River is accessible by wheelchair.
vietnamese: có thể tiếp cận bằng [phương tiện]

phrase: attracts more than [number] visitors each year
usage: Use to give a sense of a place's popularity with statistics.
example: The park attracts more than 240,000 local, interstate and international visitors each year.
vietnamese: thu hút hơn [số lượng] du khách mỗi năm

usage: Use to give context about a place's significance or reputation.
example: The Pinnacles are one of Australia's best-known landscapes.
vietnamese: một trong những… nổi tiếng nhất / lâu đời nhất của Úc

phrase: there are many different [things] to choose from
usage: Use to describe variety and options available at a place.
example: There are many different walking trails to choose from in the park.
vietnamese: có nhiều [thứ] khác nhau để lựa chọn

usage: Use to describe what an experience or place allows you to do.
example: The ferry ride provides the opportunity to see the sea lions lazing on Seal Island.
vietnamese: cung cấp cơ hội để…

usage: Use to list multiple features or examples of something.
example: The park has an array of attractions, including a koala boardwalk and a golf course.
vietnamese: một loạt [các thứ], bao gồm…

usage: Use to describe restrictions or specific zones for certain activities.
example: Diving may be enjoyed in designated areas.
vietnamese: trong các khu vực được chỉ định

phrase: The distinctive feature of X is undoubtedly…
usage: Use to highlight the most remarkable or unique characteristic of a subject.
example: The distinctive feature of this park is undoubtedly the spectacular Pinnacles.
vietnamese: Đặc điểm nổi bật của X chắc chắn là…

usage: Use to describe a large number of people coming to do something.
example: Early European settlers came in droves to swim, picnic and enjoy a day in the bush.
vietnamese: đến hàng đàn để [làm gì đó]

phrase: have been one of the focal points of the area since…
usage: Use to describe something that has been important or popular for a long time.
example: The falls have been one of the focal points of the area since the early European settlers.
vietnamese: đã là một trong những tâm điểm của khu vực kể từ…

usage: Stating business opening hours — common in advertisements and notices.
example: The library is open every weekday from 9am to 5pm.
vietnamese: Mở cửa mỗi [ngày] từ [giờ] đến [giờ].

usage: Indicating flexible availability outside regular hours.
example: The clinic is open Monday to Friday. Other times by appointment.
vietnamese: Các thời gian khác theo hẹn.

usage: Inviting groups to make reservations — common in tourism and hospitality ads.
example: We cater for all occasions. Party bookings welcome.
vietnamese: Chào đón đặt chỗ [theo nhóm].

usage: Describing a tasting or trial experience — common in food/drink tourism.
example: At the vineyard, you can sample different types of wine.
vietnamese: Nếm thử các loại [sản phẩm] khác nhau.

usage: Describing a guided visit to see how something is made.
example: Visitors can tour the chocolate factory and see how truffles are made.
vietnamese: Tham quan [cơ sở/nhà máy/xưởng].

usage: Giving a location by referencing nearby places — common in directions and addresses.
example: The campsite is located between the towns of Oxford and Reading.
vietnamese: Giữa các thị trấn [A] và [B].

phrase: Travel from [time] to [time] and participate in [activity].
usage: Describing the duration and nature of a travel or volunteer program — common in ads and brochures.
example: Travel from one week to six months and participate in a language immersion program.
vietnamese: Du lịch từ [thời gian] đến [thời gian] và tham gia vào [hoạt động].

phrase: Make a real difference by [verb+ing] in [field].
usage: Used to motivate volunteers or donors — common in charity/NGO advertising.
example: Make a real difference by teaching in underserved communities.
vietnamese: Tạo ra sự khác biệt thực sự bằng cách [động từ+ing] trong [lĩnh vực].

phrase: You could make a significant difference while [verb+ing].
usage: Combining impact with personal benefit — typical in volunteer tourism marketing.
example: You could make a significant difference while gaining valuable work experience.
vietnamese: Bạn có thể tạo ra sự khác biệt đáng kể trong khi [động từ+ing].

phrase: Do more in [period] than most people would dream about doing in a lifetime.
usage: A marketing superlative used to emphasise the intensity of an experience.
example: Do more in one year than most people would dream about doing in a lifetime.
vietnamese: Làm được nhiều thứ trong [khoảng thời gian] hơn những gì hầu hết mọi người dám mơ làm trong cả đời.

usage: Listing the best features of a tour, product, or event — very common in advertisements.
example: Highlights include: guided city tours, cooking classes, and a farewell dinner.
vietnamese: Điểm nổi bật bao gồm: [danh sách].

usage: A call to action directing people to register or apply via a website — standard in ads.
example: Apply online at www.volunteerworld.com before the closing date.
vietnamese: Đăng ký trực tuyến tại [trang web].

usage: The most common way to indicate location during a tour or giving directions.
example: Walk past the entrance and it's on your left.
vietnamese: Nó ở bên trái / phải của bạn.

phrase: If you look at the map, you'll see...
usage: Speaker introduces a location on a map. Signals that the answer is coming next.
example: If you look at the map, you'll see the library is in the northeast corner.
vietnamese: Nếu bạn nhìn vào bản đồ, bạn sẽ thấy...

phrase: You are here / We are here.
usage: Identifies the starting point on the map. Always listen for this first.
example: You are here, at the main entrance on Park Road.
vietnamese: Bạn đang ở đây / Chúng ta đang ở đây.

phrase: As you come in through the entrance...
usage: Common opening phrase when giving directions inside a building.
example: As you come in through the entrance, the reception desk is straight ahead.
vietnamese: Khi bạn đi vào qua lối vào...

usage: Indicates something is on the opposite side of an area.
example: The tennis courts are on the far side of the sports centre.
vietnamese: Ở phía bên kia của...

phrase: Take the second exit at the roundabout.
usage: Common instruction for outdoor map directions involving a roundabout.
example: At the roundabout, take the second exit onto Hill Road.
vietnamese: Rẽ ở lối ra thứ hai tại vòng xuyến.

phrase: Follow the path / road until you reach...
usage: Instruction to keep going until reaching a landmark.
example: Follow the path until you reach the lake.
vietnamese: Đi theo con đường cho đến khi bạn đến...

phrase: It's the first / second building on the left / right.
usage: Pinpoints a specific building in a sequence.
example: It's the second building on the right after the car park.
vietnamese: Đó là tòa nhà đầu tiên / thứ hai bên trái / phải.

phrase: You'll come to a junction / crossroads.
usage: Signals that a decision point is ahead.
example: You'll come to a junction — turn left there.
vietnamese: Bạn sẽ đến một ngã tư / giao lộ.

usage: A self-correction — the speaker changes their answer. This is a DISTRACTOR signal. Listen for the corrected answer.
example: The café is on the left — actually, no, I meant on the right.
vietnamese: Thực ra, không, ý tôi là...

usage: Another distractor signal — the speaker restarts their direction. The SECOND answer is correct.
example: Turn left at... sorry, let me start again. Turn right at the bank.
vietnamese: Xin lỗi, để tôi nói lại.

usage: Indicates something is exactly on the other side.
example: The bookshop is directly across from the bus station.
vietnamese: Ngay đối diện với...

usage: Speaker reassures that the location is easy to find. Often follows the key direction.
example: It's the big red building on the corner — you can't miss it.
vietnamese: Bạn không thể bỏ lỡ nó.

usage: Indicates something is hidden or not immediately visible behind another landmark.
example: The garden café is tucked away behind the main hall.
vietnamese: Nó nằm khuất phía sau...

usage: Compass-based direction, common in outdoor map descriptions.
example: Head north along the main road for about 200 metres.
vietnamese: Đi về hướng bắc / nam / đông / tây.

phrase: You can also go that way, but it's quicker to...
usage: DISTRACTOR — the speaker mentions an alternative route but then gives the preferred one. The SECOND route is the answer.
example: You can also go straight on here, past the surgery, but it's quicker to drive down Main Street.
vietnamese: Bạn cũng có thể đi lối đó, nhưng nhanh hơn nếu...

phrase: Instead of turning left, you need to turn right.
usage: DISTRACTOR — the speaker reverses a direction. Listen carefully — the corrected direction is the answer.
example: Instead of turning left at the park, turn right with the pond on your left.
vietnamese: Thay vì rẽ trái, bạn cần rẽ phải.

phrase: That's on the right; there are shops on the left.
usage: DISTRACTOR — the speaker mentions both left and right. Focus on which side the TARGET location is on, not the other landmarks.
example: The house is the second one after the bridge. That's on the right — there are shops on the left.
vietnamese: Nó ở bên phải; có các cửa hàng bên trái.

usage: Speaker clarifies or introduces a specific name, brand, or term. Listen carefully — the name that follows is often the answer.
example: It's called 'Dress Your Best' — that's the company name.
vietnamese: Nó được gọi là...

usage: Asking for someone's address or location. The answer usually includes a street name, building, or area.
example: Where are you located? — We're on Kirby Trading Estate.
vietnamese: Bạn ở đâu? / Địa chỉ của bạn ở đâu?

phrase: Could you spell that for me?
usage: A request to spell a name or word. Listen for individual letters — this is where answers are confirmed.
example: Could you spell that for me? — K-I-R-B-Y.
vietnamese: Bạn có thể đánh vần cho tôi không?

phrase: Can I take your name, please?
usage: A standard opening question in Section 1 phone conversations.
example: Can I take your name, please? — Yes, it's Sue Brown.
vietnamese: Cho tôi xin tên của bạn được không?

phrase: I'd like to place an order for...
usage: The caller states what they want to buy. The items mentioned are often answers to table completion questions.
example: I'd like to place an order for five office chairs and two glass desks.
vietnamese: Tôi muốn đặt hàng...

usage: Asking about extra costs for delivery. The answer may mention 'free delivery', 'extra charge', or a specific amount.
example: Is there a delivery charge? — No, there's no extra charge for option 2.
vietnamese: Có phí giao hàng không?

usage: DISTRACTOR — the speaker corrects a previous answer. The corrected version is the right answer.
example: The code is TG 585 — oh, actually, it should be TG 586.
vietnamese: Thực ra, nó phải là...

phrase: Let me just check that — so it's...
usage: The listener repeats back information to confirm. This repetition often contains the correct answer.
example: Let me just check that — so it's 09356 788 545?
vietnamese: Để tôi kiểm tra lại — vậy là...

usage: A product code or order number is given. Listen for a combination of letters and digits.
example: The reference number is ASP 23 — that's for the office chairs.
vietnamese: Mã tham chiếu là...

phrase: Would you like to pay by...?
usage: Asking about payment method. Common answers: credit card, debit card, cash, bank transfer.
example: Would you like to pay by credit card or bank transfer?
vietnamese: Bạn muốn thanh toán bằng...?

phrase: That comes to a total of...
usage: The speaker states the total price. Listen for the exact number and currency.
example: That comes to a total of £1,250 including delivery.
vietnamese: Tổng cộng là...

phrase: Is that with one 'l' or two?
usage: Checking spelling of names or words. Signals that spelling matters for the answer.
example: Is that with one 'l' or two? — Two l's: B-R-O-W-N-E-L-L.
vietnamese: Chữ đó có một hay hai chữ 'l'?

usage: The speaker repeats information — the repeated version confirms the correct answer.
example: Sorry, I'll just repeat that — the mobile number is 09356 788 545.
vietnamese: Xin lỗi, để tôi nhắc lại.

usage: Confirms an item is available. May contrast with 'out of stock' for other items.
example: The black chairs? Yes, we have those in stock. The grey ones are out of stock though.
vietnamese: Chúng tôi còn hàng.

usage: Giving strong advice or a recommendation. The words after this phrase are often the answer.
example: Make sure you plan your day before you set off.
vietnamese: Hãy chắc chắn rằng bạn...

phrase: The best way to get around is...
usage: Recommending a method of transport. Listen for what follows.
example: The best way to get around is on foot — don't try to drive.
vietnamese: Cách tốt nhất để di chuyển là...

usage: The speaker gives a firm recommendation. The answer often follows this phrase.
example: I'd strongly recommend wearing comfortable shoes.
vietnamese: Tôi rất khuyến khích...

usage: A reminder about something important. Signals that a key detail is coming.
example: Don't forget to check the weather the night before.
vietnamese: Đừng quên...

usage: Telling the listener not to do something themselves — someone else will do it. The role/person that follows is often the answer.
example: Leave it to the volunteers — they'll hand out water to runners.
vietnamese: Hãy để việc đó cho...

usage: Warning about something dangerous or inconvenient. What follows is what to stay away from.
example: Try to avoid the finish line area — it gets extremely crowded.
vietnamese: Cố gắng tránh...

usage: Introduces an important fact or tip. The information after this is often tested.
example: It's worth remembering that roads will be closed from 7 am.
vietnamese: Đáng nhớ rằng...

usage: DISTRACTOR — the speaker clarifies or corrects what they just said. The corrected version is the answer.
example: Bring warm clothes — what I mean is, dress in layers so you can adjust.
vietnamese: Ý tôi là...

usage: DISTRACTOR — the speaker corrects themselves. The second version is correct.
example: There are 10,000... actually, I should say 12,000 runners this year.
vietnamese: Thực ra, tôi nên nói là...

usage: Strong warning. What follows is something the listener must not do.
example: Whatever you do, don't try to cross the road while runners are passing.
vietnamese: Dù thế nào, đừng...
